text: In PennyLane's differentiable quantum programming, the ___ rule computes exact hardware gradients as d_theta f = (1/2)[f(theta + pi/2) - f(theta - pi/2)], using the quantum device itself rather than finite differences.
explanation: The parameter-shift rule yields exact analytic gradients of a QNode expectation value by evaluating the circuit at symmetrically shifted parameters — central to differentiable quantum programming. It is not a finite-difference approximation and runs on real hardware; CV versions exist for Gaussian gates with quadratic observables.
